pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## claude.ai tldraw
Use `search` to query the tldraw Editor API spec (e.g. search for methods by category or name). Use `exec` to run JavaScript on the canvas — your code receives `editor` (the tldraw Editor instance) and helpers like toRichText, createShapeId, createArrowBetweenShapes. The current canvas state is kept in model context as raw TLShape, asset, and binding data.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
The Shopify Admin API exposes hundreds of resources. The built-in tools above are optimized shortcuts for common operations (with structured output and widgets), but they only cover a subset of the API.
When the user asks about a resource that has no dedicated built-in tool — such as gift cards, metafields, metaobjects, pages, blogs, markets, translations, publications, and many others — fulfill the request with the GraphQL Workflow below. entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

Die Kapazitäten auf Netzebene 4 und die Auslastung von Umspannwerken sind nun landesweit online auf einer Karte einsehbar, was den Ausbau vor allem der Photovoltaik erleichtern soll.

Oesterreichs Energie hat mit Unterstützung der heimischen Verteilernetzbetreiber eine Karte der Netzkapazitäten als Orientierungshilfe für Anlagenbetreiber erstellt und veröffentlicht.

# Kataster Grafik SHP Dataset Summary

## License
The dataset is dual-licensed:
- **Public Access**: "Der öffentliche Zugang zu diesem Produkt unterliegt keinen Einschränkungen" (no limitations on public access)
- **Use License**: CC-BY-4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0)

## Format
ESRI Shapefile (version 1.0)

## Download URL Pattern
`https://data.bev.gv.at/download/Kataster/shp/[YYYYMMDD]/KAT_DKM_[State]_SHP_[YYYYMMDD].zip`

Example: Burgenland file for April 1, 2023 snapshot at `https://data.bev.gv.at/download/Kataster/shp/20230401/KAT_DKM_Burgenland_SHP_20230401.zip`

All nine Austrian states are available separately.

## Coordinate Reference Systems (EPSG)
- EPSG:31254
- EPSG:31255
- EPSG:31256

(Austrian Gauß-Krüger projections for different meridian strips)

## Content
The Digital Cadastral Map contains property boundaries, parcel numbers, land-use boundaries/symbols, survey control points, and state border markers across Austria.

## Update Schedule
Data maintains daily synchronization between the cadastral map and property registry. Reference date (Stichtag) indicates the snapshot date—April 1, 2023 for this version—not the original survey date.

# Digital Cadastral Map (DKM) - Key Information

## Cost & Licensing
The DKM is **not free/Open Data**. According to the page, "Die Produkte des BEV unterliegen dem Schutz des Urheberrechtsgesetzes" (BEV products are protected by copyright law). No CC BY 4.0 or similar open license is mentioned. Pricing is based on data type and usage multipliers.

## Available Formats
- **Vector**: DXF, SHP (Shapefile)
- **Raster**: PNG
- **Tabular**: CSV

GPKG format is not listed.

## Coordinate System
Data uses the Austrian Gauß-Krüger projection with the Bessel 1841 ellipsoid and MGI datum. Three zones are available (M28, M31, M34).

## Contents
The DKM includes property boundaries, parcel numbers, usage symbols, boundary points with numbers, and fixed points.

## Update Frequency
"Die zentralen Datenbestände werden für die Produktherstellung einmal täglich aktualisiert" — central data is updated once daily for product generation.

## Access/Download
Orders are placed through **BEV Shop PLUS** or the BEV Produkt-Webservice; no direct download from data.bev.gv.at is mentioned for the commercial DKM product.

## Inkrafttreten (Entry into Force)

The ElWG came into force on 24.12.2025.

## § 99: Transparenz und Reservierung verfügbarer Netzanschlusskapazitäten (Transparency and Reservation of Available Grid Connection Capacities)

Network operators must publish permissible, available, and booked grid connection capacities for electricity generation, consumption, and energy storage facilities per transformer station (network level 4), and as quickly as possible, but at the latest within three years from the entry into force of this federal law, per transformer station (network level 6) on the common internet platform according to § 117, and update them quarterly.

The grid connection capacities for electricity generation facilities must be disclosed separately by generation technology.

According to § 99 paragraph 1 ElWG, network operators must henceforth not only disclose free and reserved network capacities, but also separately identify them by generation technologies as well as for energy storage.

# § 14 Energie-Control-Gesetz (Austrian Energy Control Act)

This section details the **operational procedures of the Supervisory Board** (Aufsichtsrat) for Austria's energy regulator.

## Key Provisions:

**Governance Structure:** The Supervisory Board establishes its own rules of procedure and must meet at least quarterly or as needed.

**Meeting Requirements:** The chair must convene sessions "with at least a two-week notice following the call" and requires a minimum quorum of three members, including the chair or deputy.

**Decision-Making:** Decisions require a simple majority vote, with the chair holding a tiebreaker vote. Abstentions are prohibited.

**Documentation:** Meeting minutes must be recorded and signed by the chair, with detailed procedures outlined in the board's bylaws.

**Circular Resolutions:** These are permitted only if no member objects and require unanimous support; results must be reported at the next meeting.

**Compensation:** Board members receive "appropriate remuneration from the regulator's funds," with amounts set by the Federal Minister for Economy, Energy and Tourism.

**Current Status:** This version entered force on December 24, 2025, per Federal Law Gazette I No. 91/2025.

# Summary: Available Grid Connection Capacities for Power Generation

This LINZ NETZ GmbH webpage provides information about available network connection capacities for larger electricity generation and energy storage facilities in the Linz region.

## Key Information

**Purpose:** The page assists with site planning by showing "booked and available network connection capacities per transformer station."

**Important Disclaimers:**
- No legal claim exists for connection at a specific transformer station
- The actual operator determines the technically suitable connection point
- Available capacity data is calculated quarterly and may change daily
- "On the actual availability of the published network connection capacities there is no legal claim"

**Data Presented:**
The table lists 25 transformer stations showing:
- Booked capacity by technology type (solar, hydroelectric, thermal, storage)
- Available capacity in megavolt-amperes (MVA)
- Status as of July 27, 2026

**Notable Capacities:**
Several stations show zero availability (Baumgartenberg, Mauthausen, Rainbach, Wienerstraße), while others like Linz Industrie Bau 103 have 34.13 MVA available.

The data references Austria's standardized platform (ebUtilities) for wider regional capacity information.

# Capacity Data Format and Availability

## Data Format
The capacities are presented as a **comprehensive list** organized by individual substations (Umspannwerke), displaying booked and available capacity in MVA (megavolt-amperes) for each facility.

## Current Status
"Einmal im Quartal aktualisieren wir die gebuchten und verfügbaren Einspeisekapazitäten" — data is refreshed quarterly. The page notes: "Zuletzt aktualisiert: 3. August 2026"

## Additional Resources
Beyond the main list, the site offers:
- **Trafokarte für Einspeiser**: An interactive map allowing users to zoom into transformer stations and view capacity utilization
- **EB Utilities platform**: Austrian-wide capacity data accessible through an external link

## Important Limitations
Notably, capacities marked with an asterisk indicate facilities where "Aufgrund von Kapazitätsengpässen im Hoch- und Höchstspannungsnetz stehen derzeit keine Einspeisekapazitäten zur Verfügung" — higher-level grid constraints currently prevent new connections despite local availability.

The data reflects planned expansions through 2032, addressing infrastructure bottlenecks systematically across Lower Austria's network.

# OpenStreetMap Attribution and License Summary

Based on the German copyright page, here are the key requirements:

## Core License Terms

OpenStreetMap data is licensed under the **Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL)**. Users may "kopieren, weitergeben, zu übermitteln sowie anzupassen" (copy, distribute, transmit, and adapt) the data with proper attribution.

## Attribution Requirements

Two conditions must be met when using OSM data:

1. **Credit OpenStreetMap** by displaying the attribution notice
2. **Indicate ODbL licensing** - typically by linking to the copyright page or providing the full URL

## Share-Alike Obligation

When you modify or create derivative works from OSM data, "kannst du das Ergebnis auch nur unter derselben Lizenz weitergeben" - you must distribute the result under the identical license terms.

## Attribution Guidelines

Different presentation requirements apply depending on format (interactive maps, printed maps, static images). The page provides an example showing attribution placed in the map's corner area.

## Important Restriction

Contributors must not incorporate data from copyrighted sources like Google Maps or printed maps without explicit permission from rights holders.

# OpenStreetMap Attribution Guidelines Summary

## Key Requirements

OpenStreetMap data distributed under the Open Database License (ODbL) requires attribution when used publicly. The foundation adopted these guidelines in June 2021.

## Core Attribution Standards

Attribution must:
- Be "reasonably calculated to make any Person...aware that Content was obtained from OpenStreetMap"
- Appear in a location where users would expect to find it
- Remain legible and understandable
- Include a link to openstreetmap.org/copyright for license details

## Use-Case Specific Guidance

**Interactive Maps:** Credit typically appears in a map corner. Attribution may fade after user interaction or five seconds, but users must still access license info via an info button or menu.

**Static Images:** Multiple images on one page need only one attribution instance. Images under 100 features or covering less than 10,000 m² don't require attribution.

**Databases:** Must include ODbL text or link within the database structure, placed where users would locate documentation.

**Printed Materials:** Attribution appears beside maps, in footnotes, or acknowledgments sections, with the full URL printed out.

**Video/Film:** Attribution goes in corners, end credits, or digital descriptions (including the URL when applicable).

**Machine Learning:** Training datasets extracted from OSM are derivative databases requiring ODbL compliance. Model documentation must credit OpenStreetMap.

The guidelines emphasize these represent a "safe harbour" approach, not absolute minimums, and better attribution is always encouraged.

# Solar Energy Development Program - Styria

This webpage outlines Austria's Styria region's development program for renewable solar energy.

## Key Points

**Program Purpose:** The initiative aims to increase electricity and heat generation from renewable sources, specifically through photovoltaic expansion while protecting high-quality agricultural land and natural areas.

**Legal Status:** The ordinance was adopted June 1, 2023, and came into effect June 7, 2023 (published in Regional Law Gazette No. 52/2023). A first amendment took effect February 13, 2026.

# Grundstücksdatenbank Overview

The Grundstücksdatenbank (Property Registry Database) is an Austrian public database combining property registration records and cadastral data.

## Access & Availability

"Die Abfrage der Grundstücksdatenbank (also Grundbuch und Kataster umfassend) im Internet möglich und zwar über sogenannte Verrechnungsstellen" [accessible since 1999]. Users can also access information through the Federal Office for Metrology and Surveying's portal.

## Important Limitation

For official documents needed for government submission or legal purposes, citizens must visit district courts (property registration departments), notaries, or surveying offices—these are the only entities authorized to issue certified copies.

## Costs

Querying this database involves fees processed through designated billing agencies (Verrechnungsstellen), where users must first obtain access authorization.

## More Information

The Austrian Justice Ministry maintains a list of approved billing agencies facilitating public database access on behalf of the Federal Ministry of Justice.

# Austrian Land Registry Online Inquiry

## Access Methods

Data from Austria's property database can be queried through:

1. **JustizOnline** (Federal Ministry of Justice)
2. **Authorized billing offices** - nine private companies licensed to provide access, including firms like lexunited, MANZ, and Moody's Analytics

## Fee Structure

Costs vary by query type:

- **Full registry excerpt**: €4.89
- **Partial excerpt** (individual sections): €2.60
- **Historical records** (last 5 years): €2.44
- **Address directory searches** (up to 10 results): €1.52
- **Large area queries** (up to 2,000m radius): €63

Additional fees apply for billing office services.

## Important Notes

- "Most billing offices accept all professions and individuals" but are not legally obligated to serve all customers
- For certified excerpts required for official submission, contact a notary public
- The ÖGIZIN GmbH office exclusively serves notaries

Specific requirements for person-based searches and legal interest thresholds aren't detailed in this content.

Based on the search results, here's information about GUG § 5 Abs 4 regarding Personenverzeichnis (Person Registry) queries and the legal interest requirement:

## Legal Framework

Abschriften und Mitteilungen aus dem Personenverzeichnis (copies and information from the person registry) are provided to registered persons regarding their entries, and additionally are only provided to those persons who assert a legal interest ("rechtliches Interesse"), to the extent justified thereby.

## Who Can Access the Person Registry

According to § 5 Abs 4 GUG, access to the person registry is permitted for data protection reasons to the affected persons, i.e., those registered there regarding their data, and to other persons only if they can demonstrate a legal interest, for example, if someone has an execution title against the property owner.

## Requirements for "Legal Interest"

A legal interest must go beyond mere economic interest or interests of information, propriety, decorum or ethics, and must serve, for example, to clarify a legal relationship.

## Court Decisions on Legal Interest

Recent jurisprudence has expanded the concept somewhat. The press can have a legal interest in information through access to the person registry under § 5 Abs 4 GUG when acting in the public interest—taking into account the proportionality principle and weighing affected fundamental rights.

The court is responsible for examining whether these requirements are met, which is why such queries must be submitted to the court.

Hier sind die Ergebnisse zu Ihrer Suchanfrage zum Thema Grundbuchsdaten und Direktwerbung in Österreich:

## Öffentlichkeit des Grundbuchs und Datenschutz

Grundbuchsdaten sind in Österreich öffentlich abfragbar, und jedermann kann das Grundbuch einsehen und Abschriften oder Auszüge daraus erheben. Allerdings bedeutet dies nicht automatisch, dass diese Daten uneingeschränkt für Werbezwecke verwendbar sind.

## Datenschutzrechtliche Bewertung

Wichtig ist die Unterscheidung: Grundbuchsdaten sind personenbezogene Daten, aber nicht allgemein verfügbar. Auch wenn das Grundbuch öffentlich ist und von jedermann eingesehen werden kann, sind die Daten darin nicht allgemein verfügbar im Sinne des österreichischen Datenschutzgesetzes. Für das Grundbuch gilt Datenschutz, die Öffentlichkeit der Daten ändert hieran nichts.

## Möglichkeit der Kontaktaufnahme

Eine Kontaktaufnahme von Eigentümern bei Kaufinteresse wird grundsätzlich für möglich gehalten, und dies kann auch auf ein berechtigtes Interesse gestützt werden. Allerdings gibt es Grenzen: Eine „übermäßige" Nutzung dieser Daten ist nicht zulässig, da dann die berechtigten Interessen der betroffenen Personen überwiegen.

## Anforderungen bei Direktwerbung

Die Kontaktaufnahme muss rechtskonform sein und der Eigentümer muss auf sein datenschutzrechtliches Widerspruchsrecht hingewiesen werden.

## § 151 GewO - Adressverlage und Direktmarketingunternehmen

According to § 151 Abs. 9 GewO, the Fachverband Werbung und Marktkommunikation (Advertising and Marketing Communications Association) has the obligation to maintain a Robinson list where people can register for free to exclude themselves from receiving personally addressed advertising material.

## Robinsonliste (Robinson List)

Registration in the Robinson List means that no personally addressed advertising material from Austrian address brokers and direct marketing companies will be sent or distributed to you. The list is updated monthly by the Fachverband Werbung und Marktkommunikation and made available to companies with the "address brokers and direct marketing companies" business license.

## Legal Framework

§ 151 GewO contains stricter requirements compared to EU law and applies exclusively to Austrian address brokers and direct marketing companies. The Robinson List only takes effect against "address brokers and direct marketing companies."

# Summary: Direct Marketing and Postal Mailings by Real Estate Developers

## Key Decision
The Austrian Data Protection Authority (DSB) ruled on April 23, 2019 (GZ DSB-D123.626/0006-DSB/2018) that "a single postal mailing to consumers is permissible."

## When Postal Direct Marketing is Permissible

Single postal mailings to property owners based on land registry data are lawful when:

- Data sourced from publicly accessible land registers
- Used only once for direct marketing purposes
- Recipients offered opportunity to opt-out and request deletion
- No disproportionality exists between sender's interests and recipient's privacy rights

## Important Distinctions

**Published data retains DSGVO protection.** Simply because information is publicly available doesn't eliminate data protection requirements. When publicly available data is enriched—such as combining registry information with acquisition campaigns—this constitutes "processing" requiring a lawful basis under Article 6 DSGVO.

**Email differs from postal mail.** Email marketing requires recipient consent (§107 TKG), with narrow exceptions for existing customers. Postal campaigns face lower restrictions.

## Limiting Factor

Multiple mailings in short timeframes could be deemed disproportionate, potentially rendering the practice unlawful despite a single mailing being acceptable.

# Grundbuchsdaten und Direktwerbung: Zulässigkeit

## Kernaussagen zum BVwG-Fall

**Kontaktaufnahme grundsätzlich möglich:**
Die Kontaktaufnahme mit Grundbucheigentümern bei Kaufinteresse ist zulässig und kann auf berechtigte Interessen gestützt werden (Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO).

**Rechtsgrundlage erforderlich:**
Werden Grundbuchsdaten in eigene Datenbanken übertragen, benötigt dies eine separate rechtliche Grundlage gemäß Art. 6 Abs. 1 DSGVO.

**Datenschutz trotz Öffentlichkeit:**
"Auch wenn das Grundbuch öffentlich ist…sind die Daten im nicht allgemein verfügbar." Öffentlichkeit negiert Datenschutzverpflichtungen nicht.

**Grenzen der Datenoffenlegung:**
Die Sichtbarmachung von Liegenschaftsdaten in Briefen verstößt gegen Datenschutz. Betroffene erwarten vernünftigerweise nicht, dass solche Informationen "Dritten offen vor Augen geführt werden."

## Erforderliche Maßnahmen

- Informationspflichten nach Art. 14 DSGVO erfüllen
- Widerspruchsrechte der Betroffenen hinweisen
- Datenoffenlegung bei Versand minimieren
- Datenschutzrechtliche Prüfung vor Datenbanknutzung

# Robinsonliste: Who Must Comply

## Applicable Businesses

The Robinsonliste applies **exclusively to Austrian "address retailers and direct marketing companies"** ("Adressverlage und Direktmarketingunternehmen"). 

The regulation does not extend to other enterprises with different business licenses. As the document states: "Advertising mailings by entrepreneurs with a different business license or anonymous postal shipments fall outside the Robinsonliste regime."

This means advertising agencies, market researchers, PR consultants, and trading companies cannot legally obtain or use the list, even if they conduct some direct marketing activities.

## Access and Updates

The professional association for advertising (Fachverband Werbung und Marktkommunikation) maintains the list and must "update it monthly and provide it to companies with the business license for address retailers and direct marketing companies."

The document specifies that the association "provides the Robinsonliste exclusively to Austrian address retailers and direct marketing enterprises" to comply with legal obligations.

## Key Restriction

The list cannot be shared with companies located outside Austria, even within the EU, without explicit consent from registered individuals regarding international data transfers.

## Key Provisions:

**Telephone Calls & Faxes for Advertising:**
Calls – including the sending of faxes – for advertising purposes without prior consent of the user are impermissible. Consent from a person authorized by the end user to use their connection is equivalent to user consent. Given consent can be revoked at any time; revocation of consent has no effect on a contractual relationship with the recipient of the consent.

**Electronic Mail (Email & SMS) for Direct Advertising:**
The sending of electronic mail – including SMS – is impermissible without prior consent of the recipient if the sending is for purposes of direct advertising.

**Exceptions to Consent Requirement:**
Consent is not necessary when the sender obtained the contact information in connection with the sale or a service to their customers and the message is for direct advertising of their own similar products or services, provided the customer clearly and distinctly has the opportunity to refuse such use of contact information at collection and additionally with each transmission free of charge and without difficulty.

**Caller ID Display:**
With advertising calls, the caller must not suppress or falsify the caller number display and the service provider must not be instructed to do so.

This regulation represents a restrictive approach to unsolicited advertising communications in Austria.

## Key Information

According to § 14e of the Energiewirtschaftsgesetz (EnWG), all electricity distribution network operators are required to establish and operate a common internet platform. The internet platform VNBdigital.de has been live since January 1, 2023.

## Functions and Requirements

§ 14e EnWG obligates electricity distribution network operators to establish and operate a common internet platform starting in 2023 with graduated functionalities including access to network connection information, technical connection terms, and publication of regional planning documents.

As of January 1, 2025, distribution network operators must ensure that anyone has free access to the technical connection conditions according to § 19 Paragraph 1 via the common internet platform.

## Publication Requirements

Distribution network operators publish on the common internet platform at minimum: the respective regional scenario according to § 14d Paragraph 3 within four weeks of completion, the respective network expansion plan according to § 14d Paragraph 1 within four weeks of completion, and the statements according to § 14d Paragraph 6.

## Usage Conditions

Since March 1, 2021, swisstopo's digital standard products, such as digital maps, aerial images and landscape models, are provided free of charge as Open Government Data and can be used freely. For digital or analog representations and publications as well as for data sharing, one of the following source attributions must be provided: "Bundesamt für Landestopografie swisstopo".

Regarding attribution format, the ideal approach is to provide the source next to the swisstopo data each time it appears, while an acceptable alternative is to list the source centrally on a webpage that lists all sources used in the map application or service, with a link (URL or hyperlink) to the source webpage in the map application or in the description of the web service.

## swissALTI3D Specifics

swissALTI3D is a highly precise digital elevation model which describes the surface of Switzerland without vegetation and development, and is updated in a 6-year refresh cycle.

# Veröffentlichungspflichten nach § 14e EnWG

Basierend auf dem Gesetzestext müssen folgende Informationen auf der gemeinsamen Internetplattform veröffentlicht werden:

**Erforderliche Veröffentlichungen (ab den genannten Terminen):**

1. **Ab 1. Januar 2024:** Verlinkung zu Netzbetreiber-Webseiten für Netzanschlussbegehren und erforderliche Informationen gemäß § 8 EEG und § 18 EnWG

2. **Ab 1. Januar 2025:** „kostenlosen Zugang zu den technischen Anschlussbedingungen nach § 19 Absatz 1 sowie zu den Begründungen der Ergänzungen"

3. **Dauerhaft:** „das jeweilige Regionalszenario nach § 14d Absatz 3, spätestens vier Wochen nach Fertigstellung, den jeweiligen Netzausbauplan nach § 14d Absatz 1, spätestens vier Wochen nach Fertigstellung und die Stellungnahmen nach § 14d Absatz 6"

**Wichtig:** Der Wortlaut nennt **keine expliziten Angaben zu Netzanschlusskapazität oder verfügbaren Kapazitäten**. Diese könnten durch Festlegungen der Regulierungsbehörde nach § 29 Absatz 1 konkretisiert werden.

# MaStR Data Download Summary

**License:** "Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung – Version 2.0" (Data License Germany – Attribution – Version 2.0)

**Format:** XML

**Update Schedule:** The dataset is typically refreshed daily at 5:00 AM with the current data status. Historical exports from specific reference dates are also available.

**Current Data Stand:** Last updated September 30, 2026 at 00:00:00

**File Size:** Approximately 3.14 GB (compressed as ZIP)

**Download URL:** `https://download.marktstammdatenregister.de/Gesamtdatenexport_20260930_26.1.zip`

The Marktstammdatenregister (Market Master Data Register) provides comprehensive public data exports from Germany's energy market registry, maintained by the Bundesnetzagentur (Federal Network Agency). The service is designed primarily for advanced IT users, with simpler options available through the website's public unit and market actor overviews.

# Swiss Official Survey Data (Amtliche Vermessung) - Access Overview

## Availability by Canton

The page indicates two access categories:

- **Freely Available**: Cantons without notation can use service links without ordering
- **Registration/Approval Required**: Cantons marked with "(1)" require registration; those marked "(2)" need approval before access

All 26 cantons plus Liechtenstein (LI) are listed with Version 24.0 data available.

## Data Formats Offered

Multiple formats are provided: INTERLIS (canton-wise), GeoPackage, ESRI Shapefile, DXF, CSV, IFC, WFS, WMS, and OGC API Features.

## Coordinate System

While not explicitly stated on this page, Swiss geodata typically uses **EPSG:2056** (Swiss LV95 projection) as the standard.

## Usage Terms

The page notes: "For cantons with 'Freely available' status, the service links can be used without ordering. However, cantonal usage conditions must be observed."

## DXF and Utility Data Restrictions

"Data in DXF format are only available for cantons that have enabled the format" and "contain only data released by responsible network operators." Maximum 10 extracts daily per user; unsuitable for construction projects.

## Landowner Data

The page does not specifically address ownership data restrictions or privacy limitations regarding property owner information.

## Dataset Overview

sonnendach.ch is a dataset on opendata.swiss that shows for a roof how well it is suited for solar energy use and what yield would be possible. The interactive application www.sonnendach.ch informs about the suitability of residential roofs for solar energy use and communicates simply how much solar electricity or heat could be produced with a residential roof.

## Organization and License

The dataset is provided by the Federal Office of Energy (BFE). It is available for free use with source attribution required.

## Data Calculation

The sun's path over the year is simulated and the solar radiation hitting each roof surface is calculated based on values from the Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology (MeteoSchweiz) and 3D building data from the Federal Office of Topography swisstopo (swissBUILDINGS3D 2.0).

## Download Formats

The dataset is available in multiple formats including GeoPackage (GPKG) for roofs with monthly values, along with WMS/WMTS services and API access.

GeoPackage data is available for download through opendata.swiss.

The Umweltbundesamt GmbH publishes comprehensive protected area geodata on data.gv.at. The data contains nature conservation protection categories compiled from federal state INSPIRE services, including national parks, European protected areas, nature reserves, landscape protection areas, etc.

## Wesentliche Erkenntnisse

Die Suche zeigt, dass Deutschland durch die EnWG-Novelle 2025 neue Regelungen zur Transparenz bei Netzanschlusskapazitäten implementiert, die mit der Umsetzung der Richtlinie 2019/944 verbunden sind.

### Veröffentlichungspflicht für Verteilnetzbetreiber

Ein neuer § 17c EnWG-E verpflichtet die Netzbetreiber, verfügbare Netzkapazitäten auf einer geografischen Karte monatlich aktualisiert im Internet zu veröffentlichen. Netzbetreiber sollen Netzanschlusskapazitäten auf geografischen Karten ausweisen und monatlich aktualisiert auf ihrer Internetseite verfügbar machen.

### Umsetzung der EU-Richtlinie 2019/944

Nach der im Mai 2024 beschlossenen Novelle der Elektrizitätsbinnenmarktrichtlinie (Art. 31, Abs. 2 und 3 neu) sind Verteilnetzbetreiber dazu verpflichtet, Informationen über die in ihrem Netzgebiet für neue Anschlüsse verfügbare Kapazität zu veröffentlichen.

### Kapazitätskarte und Inhalte

Netzbetreiber sind verpflichtet, verfügbare und reservierte Netzanschlusskapazitäten monatlich auf ihrer Webseite zu veröffentlichen. Auf die tatsächliche Verfügbarkeit der veröffentlichten Netzanschlusskapazitäten besteht kein Rechtsanspruch.

Die Regelungen zielt darauf ab, mehr Transparenz im Netzanschlussverfahren zu schaffen, insbesondere für Einspeiser und zur besseren Informiertheit von Anschlussnehmern.

The data is managed by Department RU7 - Department of Spatial Planning and Overall Transport.

### Kärnten - Photovoltaik Freiflächen Verordnung und KAGIS Geodaten

**Verordnung und Eignungszonen:**

Die Kärntner Photovoltaikanlagen-Verordnung ist am 15. August 2024 in Kraft getreten und hat das Ziel, einerseits klare Definitionen von Freiflächenanlagen und andererseits den beschleunigten Ausbau der Gewinnung erneuerbarer Energie aus Sonnenkraft zu erreichen. Mit der neuen Verordnung wird erstmals zwischen Agri-Photovoltaikanlagen und sonstigen Freiflächenanlagen auf Grünland unterschieden.

**Ausschlussbereiche und Geodaten:**

Böden mit mangelnder Standorteignung können im KAGIS im Reiter Raumordnung-Flächenwidmung nachverfolgt werden. Insbesondere betrifft dies rote und rot-gelbe Zonen (Gefahrenzonen), braune Zonen (Untergrundbeschaffenheit), dunkelviolette Zonen (Oberflächenwasser) sowie die Trinkwasserversorgung (engeres Schutzgebiet).

**KAGIS Datenbereitstellung:**

Im Sinne der OpenGovernment-Initiative stellt KAGIS sukzessive Geodaten kostenfrei zum freien Download zur Verfügung. Mit dem KAGIS Onlinebestellformular können Sie KAGIS Geodaten und Karten bestellen. Bestellungen von KAGIS-Produkten werden ausnahmslos über das Onlinebestellformular abgewickelt.

---

**SAGIS Geodatenportal:**

Das Salzburger Geographische Informationssystem (SAGIS) ist eine Serviceeinrichtung des Landes Salzburg und bietet ein Informationssystem zur Bereitstellung von Geodaten und Geodiensten. Das SAGIS bietet eine Reihe von Geodaten, Karten und Daten zum freien Download an. Bei den Basis-Geodaten handelt es sich um landesweite Datensätze, die unter der Angabe der Quelle (Land Salzburg) frei verwendet werden dürfen.

**Photovoltaik und Solarpotenzial:**

Das Land Salzburg bietet als kostenlose Serviceleistung das exakte Solarpotenzial für Ihr Gebäude im Geodatenviewer des Landes SAGISOnline. Hier erkennen Sie, welche Flächen prinzipiell für eine Solarnutzung geeignet sind. Im SAGISonline kann jede/r das Solarpotenzial seiner Liegenschaft abfragen und hat somit eine gute Entscheidungsgrundlage für die Anschaffung einer Photovoltaikanlage, weil der jährliche Energieertrag relativ genau berechnet werden kann.

**Kostenlose Bereitstellung:**

Das Land Salzburg bietet SAGISonline unentgeltlich an.

# ALKIS Data and Open Data Status

**Are ALKIS parcel records (vector with parcel numbers) Open Data?**

No. The Bavarian survey administration does not provide ALKIS parcel data ("Flurstücksinformationen aus ALKIS, einschließlich der Grenzpunktinformationen") as open data. These remain subject to fees according to state surveying law.

**Which ALKIS products are freely available?**

The administration offers certain cadastral excerpts as open data, including:
- ALKIS parcel map (raster image without parcel numbers)
- ALKIS actual land use
- ALKIS administrative areas
- Building outlines and 3D building models

**License and Attribution**

Free datasets use the CC BY 4.0 license. The required attribution reads:

*"Bayerische Vermessungsverwaltung – www.geodaten.bayern.de"*

A complete example: *"Geobasisdaten: Bayerische Vermessungsverwaltung – www.geodaten.bayern.de (Daten verändert), Lizenz: CC BY 4.0"*

### 12. Grundbuch und Direktwerbung (AT). Das ist keine Rechtsberatung.

**Zugang und Kosten** (**V**)
- Über JustizOnline oder zugelassene Verrechnungsstellen. oesterreich.gv.at nennt neun Stellen (u. a. lexunited, MANZ, Moody's Analytics), ÖGIZIN nur für Notare. Andere Quellen sprechen von zehn Stellen inklusive der Notarstelle.
- Gebühren laut oesterreich.gv.at:
  - vollständiger Auszug 4,89 €
  - Teilauszug 2,60 €
  - historisch (5 Jahre) 2,44 €
  - Adressverzeichnis 1,52 €
  - Umkreisabfrage 63 €
  - Die Verrechnungsstellen schlagen eigene Entgelte auf.
- Laut Snippet gelten die Gebühren seit 01.08.2026 (**T**).
- Belege: https://www.oesterreich.gv.at/de/themen/bauen_und_wohnen/grundstueckskauf_und_grundbuch/grundbuch/Seite.600340 · https://www.justiz.gv.at/html/default/2c9484852308c2a601240b4acb4b0842.de.html

**Suche nach Person**
- Die maßgebliche Norm ist § 5 Abs. 4 GUG, nicht § 6 (**V**). Wer nicht selbst eingetragen ist, bekommt Auskunft aus dem Personenverzeichnis nur bei „rechtlichem Interesse“. Eine Ablehnung ergeht per Gerichtsbeschluss.
- Wirtschaftliches Interesse reicht nicht (**T**, OGH 5 Ob 178/22w).
- Die Abfrage nach Grundstück (EZ/GST) über das Hauptbuch ist frei.
- Beleg: https://www.jusline.at/gesetz/gug/paragraf/5

**Direktwerbung**
- DSB, 23.04.2019, GZ DSB-D123.626/0006-DSB/2018: Eine **einmalige** postalische Zusendung an Eigentümer auf Basis von Grundbuchdaten ist nach Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO zulässig (**V**, Sekundärquelle dataprotect.at). Bedingungen:
  - Widerspruchs- und Löschmöglichkeit
  - keine Unverhältnismäßigkeit; mehrfache Zusendungen in kurzer Zeit können unzulässig werden
- Weitere Punkte laut Sekundärquellen (**V**, Geuer RA zu einem BVwG-Fall):
  - Grundbuchdaten gelten nicht als „allgemein verfügbar“.
  - Die Übernahme in eigene Datenbanken braucht eine eigene Rechtsgrundlage.
  - Art. 14 DSGVO (Informationspflicht) ist zu erfüllen.
  - Liegenschaftsdaten dürfen im Brief nicht für Dritte sichtbar sein.
- **§ 174 TKG 2021**: Werbeanrufe, E-Mail und SMS brauchen vorherige Einwilligung, mit Ausnahme für Bestandskunden (**T**). Für Briefe gilt die Vorschrift nicht.
- **Robinsonliste nach § 151 GewO**: bindet **nur** Adressverlage und Direktmarketingunternehmen und wird nur an diese abgegeben. Andere Gewerbe können sie nicht beziehen (**V**).
- Belege: https://www.dataprotect.at/2019/06/29/direktmarketing-und-postalische-zusendungen-durch-immobilienentwickler/ · https://www.geuer.at/2023/12/03/grundbuch-datenschutz/ · https://www.wko.at/information-consulting/werbung-marktkommunikation/robinsonliste-eintragung--bezug--rechte-und-pflichten

- **Bayern**: Flurstücke als Vektor mit Nummern sind **kein** Open Data und bleiben gebührenpflichtig (**V**).
  - Frei sind: Parzellarkarte (Raster ohne Flurstücksnummern), Tatsächliche Nutzung, Verwaltungsgebiete, Gebäude und LoD2 unter CC BY 4.0.
  - Attribution: „Bayerische Vermessungsverwaltung – www.geodaten.bayern.de“.
  - Seit Juli 2026 stehen Parzellarkarte und Uraufnahme unter CC BY 4.0 (**V**).
  - Belege: https://www.geodaten.bayern.de/odd/m/3/html/faq.html · https://geodatenonline.bayern.de/geodatenonline/seiten/aktuell
- **MaStR Gesamtdatenexport** (**V**):
  - Lizenz „Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung – Version 2.0“.
  - XML im ZIP (rund 3,14 GB), täglich gegen 5 Uhr aktualisiert.
  - Aktuelle Datei: `https://download.marktstammdatenregister.de/Gesamtdatenexport_20260930_26.1.zip`
  - Beleg: https://www.marktstammdatenregister.de/MaStR/Datendownload
- **Netzkapazitäten**:
  - § 14e EnWG (VNBdigital) verlangt dem Wortlaut nach **keine** Kapazitätsangaben. Pflicht sind Links zu Netzanschlussbegehren (ab 2024), TAB (ab 2025) sowie Regionalszenarien und Netzausbaupläne (**V**, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/enwg_2005/__14e.html).
  - Ein **§ 17c EnWG-E** („Netzanschlusspaket“) sieht eine geografische Karte der verfügbaren Kapazität an der Umspannebene HS/MS vor, monatlich aktualisiert. Es gibt Referentenentwürfe (Jan./Apr. 2026) und BT-Drs. 21/7866 vom 07.09.2026 (**T**).
  - Ob das Gesetz inzwischen in Kraft ist: **NV**. Nach meinem Stand ist es ein Entwurf.
  - EU-Grundlage: Art. 31 Abs. 3 RL 2019/944 in der Fassung von 2024 (**T**).

### 13b. Schweiz

- **geodienste.ch Amtliche Vermessung** (Version 24.0) (**V**):
  - Formate: INTERLIS, GPKG, SHP, DXF, CSV, IFC, WFS, WMS, OGC API Features.

  - EPSG:2056 ist üblich, auf der Seite aber nicht genannt (**NV**).
  - Beleg: https://www.geodienste.ch/downloads/av?locale=de
- **swisstopo OGD** (seit 01.03.2021 kostenlos, also auch swissALTI3D):

  - Beleg: https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/de/nutzungsbedingungen-kostenlose-geodaten-und-geodienste
- **BFE sonnendach/sonnenfassade**: auf opendata.swiss mit GPKG, WMS/WMTS und Quellenangabe-Pflicht (**T**). Die Seite gab 403. https://opendata.swiss/de/dataset/eignung-von-hausdachern-fur-die-nutzung-von-sonnenenergie
- **CH-Netzbetreiberkapazitäten**: **NV**.

---

### Kernaussagen für die Umsetzung

1. Die DKM mit Grundstücksnummern und KG ist als **Stichtags-GPKG unter CC BY 4.0 frei**. Das gilt aber nicht für den tagesaktuellen Stand, die Shop-Produkte und den INSPIRE-WFS.
2. Einheitlich CC BY 4.0 sind: INVEKOS, basemap.at, VGD, BEV-DLM-Bauwerke, ALS-DGM 1 m, EEA Natura 2000/NatDA und Flächenwidmung OÖ.
3. Die Netzkapazitäten in AT sind öffentlich, aber **nicht maschinenlesbar und ohne Lizenz**. Einen API- oder Datenzugang sollte man bei ebUtilities oder Oesterreichs Energie anfragen.
4. OSM kommt mit ODbL-Share-Alike. Aus OSM abgeleitete Datenbanken sollten daher von den proprietären Anreicherungen getrennt gehalten werden.
5. Eigentümer-Ansprache: Suche nur über Grundstück, nicht über die Person (§ 5 Abs. 4 GUG). Brief einmalig, mit Art-14-Information und Widerspruchshinweis. Kein E-Mail- oder Telefonkontakt ohne Einwilligung.

Offene Punkte zur Nachprüfung: § 99 ElWG im Volltext bei RIS, Status von § 17c EnWG, SAPRO-PV-Geodaten der Steiermark, Nutzungsbedingungen von ebUtilities, Lizenz des NÖ-PV-Zonen-Datensatzes und die Länderwerte der DE-ALKIS-Tabelle.

**Zugang und Kosten** (**V**)
- Über JustizOnline oder zugelassene Verrechnungsstellen. oesterreich.gv.at nennt neun Stellen (u. a. lexunited, MANZ, Moody's Analytics), ÖGIZIN nur für Notare. Andere Quellen sprechen von zehn Stellen inklusive der Notarstelle.

  - Teilauszug 2,60 €
  - historisch (5 Jahre) 2,44 €
  - Adressverzeichnis 1,52 €

  - Die Verrechnungsstellen schlagen eigene Entgelte auf.
- Laut Snippet gelten die Gebühren seit 01.08.2026 (**T**).
- Belege: https://www.oesterreich.gv.at/de/themen/bauen_und_wohnen/grundstueckskauf_und_grundbuch/grundbuch/Seite.600340 · https://www.justiz.gv.at/html/default/2c9484852308c2a601240b4acb4b0842.de.html

**Suche nach Person**
- Die maßgebliche Norm ist § 5 Abs. 4 GUG, nicht § 6 (**V**). Wer nicht selbst eingetragen ist, bekommt Auskunft aus dem Personenverzeichnis nur bei „rechtlichem Interesse“. Eine Ablehnung ergeht per Gerichtsbeschluss.
- Wirtschaftliches Interesse reicht nicht (**T**, OGH 5 Ob 178/22w).
- Die Abfrage nach Grundstück (EZ/GST) über das Hauptbuch ist frei.
- Beleg: https://www.jusline.at/gesetz/gug/paragraf/5

**Direktwerbung**
- DSB, 23.04.2019, GZ DSB-D123.626/0006-DSB/2018: Eine **einmalige** postalische Zusendung an Eigentümer auf Basis von Grundbuchdaten ist nach Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO zulässig (**V**, Sekundärquelle dataprotect.at). Bedingungen:
  - Widerspruchs- und Löschmöglichkeit
  - keine Unverhältnismäßigkeit; mehrfache Zusendungen in kurzer Zeit können unzulässig werden
- Weitere Punkte laut Sekundärquellen (**V**, Geuer RA zu einem BVwG-Fall):
  - Grundbuchdaten gelten nicht als „allgemein verfügbar“.
  - Die Übernahme in eigene Datenbanken braucht eine eigene Rechtsgrundlage.
  - Art. 14 DSGVO (Informationspflicht) ist zu erfüllen.
  - Liegenschaftsdaten dürfen im Brief nicht für Dritte sichtbar sein.
- **§ 174 TKG 2021**: Werbeanrufe, E-Mail und SMS brauchen vorherige Einwilligung, mit Ausnahme für Bestandskunden (**T**). Für Briefe gilt die Vorschrift nicht.
- **Robinsonliste nach § 151 GewO**: bindet **nur** Adressverlage und Direktmarketingunternehmen und wird nur an diese abgegeben. Andere Gewerbe können sie nicht beziehen (**V**).
- Belege: https://www.dataprotect.at/2019/06/29/direktmarketing-und-postalische-zusendungen-durch-immobilienentwickler/ · https://www.geuer.at/2023/12/03/grundbuch-datenschutz/ · https://www.wko.at/information-consulting/werbung-marktkommunikation/robinsonliste-eintragung--bezug--rechte-und-pflichten

### Kernaussagen für die Umsetzung

1. Die DKM mit Grundstücksnummern und KG ist als **Stichtags-GPKG unter CC BY 4.0 frei**. Das gilt aber nicht für den tagesaktuellen Stand, die Shop-Produkte und den INSPIRE-WFS.
2. Einheitlich CC BY 4.0 sind: INVEKOS, basemap.at, VGD, BEV-DLM-Bauwerke, ALS-DGM 1 m, EEA Natura 2000/NatDA und Flächenwidmung OÖ.
3. Die Netzkapazitäten in AT sind öffentlich, aber **nicht maschinenlesbar und ohne Lizenz**. Einen API- oder Datenzugang sollte man bei ebUtilities oder Oesterreichs Energie anfragen.
4. OSM kommt mit ODbL-Share-Alike. Aus OSM abgeleitete Datenbanken sollten daher von den proprietären Anreicherungen getrennt gehalten werden.
5. Eigentümer-Ansprache: Suche nur über Grundstück, nicht über die Person (§ 5 Abs. 4 GUG). Brief einmalig, mit Art-14-Information und Widerspruchshinweis. Kein E-Mail- oder Telefonkontakt ohne Einwilligung.

Offene Punkte zur Nachprüfung: § 99 ElWG im Volltext bei RIS, Status von § 17c EnWG, SAPRO-PV-Geodaten der Steiermark, Nutzungsbedingungen von ebUtilities, Lizenz des NÖ-PV-Zonen-Datensatzes und die Länderwerte der DE-ALKIS-Tabelle.

I've handed the full source report (about 2,500 words, in German with URLs) back to you. Each entry is marked as checked on the source page itself, taken only from search-result snippets, or not verified. No files were written.

**Freely usable (CC BY 4.0), checked on the source page:**

The national GeoPackage for 1 April 2025 is about 34 GB in EPSG:31287. The daily-updated version, the BEV shop products and the INSPIRE WFS carry BEV fees and terms.
- **Also CC BY 4.0:**
  - AMA INVEKOS field plots: GeoPackage, OGC API Features, two releases a year; newest confirmed is 2025-1.
  - BEV administrative boundaries.
  - BEV 1 m laser-scan terrain model; the dataset record I opened is dated 15.09.2019.
  - EEA Natura 2000 (end 2024) and EEA nationally designated areas (August 2025).
  - Upper Austria zoning plans, attributed as "Datenquelle: Land Oö., doris.at".
- **BEV building dataset (DLM Bauwerke):** confirmed free of charge; the CC BY 4.0 licence comes only from a search snippet.
- **basemap.at:** attribution is "Grundkarte: basemap.at" or "Datenquelle: basemap.at", linked to basemap.at. The current tile domain is `mapsneu.wien.gv.at/basemap/...`, and the capabilities file lists the four layers you named.

**Grid capacities in Austria:**
- They are public but not machine-readable and carry no licence. Netz NÖ, Energienetze Steiermark, Salzburg Netz and Linz Netz publish HTML tables or maps with 2026 dates and state there is no legal claim to the capacity. APG shows a table dated 1 August 2026 and says no unrestricted capacity is currently available anywhere in its grid.
- ebUtilities, the nationwide map, couldn't be read automatically, so its terms and any download option are unknown.
- Not found: Netz Oberösterreich (only its 2026 grid development plan PDF), Netz Burgenland, Wiener Netze, KNG-Kärnten Netz and TINETZ.
- The publication duty is § 99 of the new Electricity Act (ElWG), in force since 24.12.2025. I only confirmed the section title; its content comes from search snippets.

**Owner contact (not legal advice):**
- Owners can't be looked up by name without a "legal interest". The rule is § 5 (4) GUG, not § 6. Looking up by parcel is free; a full extract costs €4.89.
- A 2019 Data Protection Authority decision (reported by a secondary source) allows a one-off letter to owners based on land-register data, citing Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. It must offer an objection and deletion option and meet the Art. 14 information duty.
- Email, SMS and phone advertising need prior consent under § 174 TKG 2021. The Robinson list only binds address publishers and direct-marketing firms.

**Germany and Switzerland:**
- Per a 2025 conference talk (search snippet only), 15 of 16 German states publish parcels as open data. Bavaria doesn't: its parcel vectors with numbers remain paid.
- The German grid-connection platform law (§ 14e EnWG) doesn't require capacity figures. A capacity-map duty (§ 17c) is still a bill; I found no sign it has passed.
- The German plant register (MaStR) export is under Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung 2.0 and updated daily.
- Switzerland: swisstopo data is free for commercial use with the credit "©swisstopo". Cadastral data on geodienste.ch is free, registration-only or approval-only depending on the canton.

**Still unverified:** the wording of § 99 ElWG, the Styria PV priority zones as downloadable data, the ebUtilities terms, the licence of the Lower Austria PV-zone dataset, the individual German state values, and Swiss grid-capacity publications.
